newsitem.title: ITALY: Bank of Italy seen selling marks at 995.50 lire.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Italy seen selling marks at 995.50 lire.

text.p: The Bank of Italy was seen selling marks for lire at 995.50 on Tuesday, foreign exchange dealers said.
The lira was quoted at 995.20/5.55 per mark at 1405 GMT, weaker than its central rate in Europe's exchange rate mechanism of 990 per mark.
"The Bank of Italy were definitely selling marks at 995.50 earlier," one trader at a London-based bank said.
Another trader here said: "They intervened several times at 995.40 and 995.50."
"The Bank of Italy doesn't like these levels and it's probable that it intervened in defence of the lira to take the tops off the peaks of the mark," another dealer here said.
Others however, said they had only heard the Italian central bank was checking rates in the market and were unable to confirm whether it had been propping up the lira or not.
Traders talked about waves of mark buying which had weakened the lira gradually to around 996 from around 992 this morning.
